text:
nora: Quick follow-up from design review: we've had reports that the approval UX for eval runs is ambiguous when mixed results exist (some regressions, some improvements). Users accidentally approve entire prompt-sets when they only meant to approve a specific run. Screenshot: https://screens.redwood.ai/mix-results.png

diego: Oh no. We should clearly separate "Approve run" vs "Approve prompt-set" actions and avoid promoting the global approve as the default.

mei: Agreed. Can we change the primary CTA in the diff header to "Approve run" and move "Approve prompt-set" to a tertiary menu? That should reduce accidental bulk approvals.

lucas: Also, for bulk actions we need an explicit scope confirmation UI. Not a modal by default, but a small confirmation drawer that summarizes what will be approved (counts + types) with a single checkbox "I confirm I want to approve X runs" for destructive bulk approves.

nora: I like the drawer approach. Less disruptive than modal, still stops accidents. For single-run approves the inline snackbar undo is fine.

diego: Accessibility point: screenreader users need clear announcements about scope. When a user triggers bulk approve, assertive live region should read: "Approving 12 runs in prompt-set \u2014 4 regressions, 8 improvements. Confirm to continue."

mei: Good call. Also include an accessible summary inside the drawer with a table-like list: run name + status icon + short reason string. Keep it short so SR users can scan.

lucas: For keyboard shortcuts we should avoid mapping a single key to approve. Maybe require a combo (Shift+A) for approve and when used in a filtered view it approves only visible items. We must make the scope explicit in the live announcement.

nora: Implementation detail: when approving visible items show a tiny inline label on the approve CTA like "Approve visible (3)". If the user has a selection, label becomes "Approve selected (5)". Make these accessible via aria-label and visible text.

diego: Copy nit: prefer verbs-first in toast: "Approved 3 runs 14 Undo". That helps users scanning notifications. Also ensure translation tokens support reordering for languages where verb comes after object.

mei: Audit requirement: every approve must create an entry in the audit trail with actor, timestamp, and scope. Add a small link "View audit" in the snackbar that opens the audit pane focused on that entry.

lucas: Nice. For the snackbar link, make sure it is keyboard-focusable and that activation doesn't steal focus from the main workflow. It should open a side pane but leave focus on the current diff unless user tabs into the pane.

nora: Edge case: if a user approves while the list is filtered (e.g., quality-only), should the audit entry note the filter? I think yes, include filter context so reviewers can see what was actually approved.

diego: Agree. Include a small json blob in the audit entry with filter keys (quality:true, latency:false, selectedIds:[...]) for clarity. Make sure PII is not included.

mei: A11y nit: when opening the drawer confirmation, move focus into the drawer and land on the heading that reads the scope. When drawer closes return focus to the approve CTA. Use focus management helpers.

lucas: Also throttle live region announcements so they don't repeat if the user toggles filters quickly. Debounce 300ms and only announce on confirmed actions or when the drawer opens.

nora: Action items: nora -> update Figma with drawer confirm pattern and new CTA labels; diego -> a11y spec for live region copy and focus management; mei -> backend audit schema + snackbar "View audit" link; lucas -> implement shortcut mapping to Shift+A and visual hint chip on focus.

ux-bot: created task PROD-5010 "Eval approvals: explicit scope, drawer confirm, audit trail" (https://tasks.redwood.ai/5010) assigned to nora, diego, mei, lucas

diego: tiny UX polish: show an inline mini-summary above the drawer with icon badges: regressions, improvements, cost-up, cost-down so users can immediately scan counts before expanding drawer.

mei: Good idea. I'll add the badges to Figma and include localized tooltip text for each metric.

lucas: One last thing: telemetry event names: approval_initiated, approval_confirmed, approval_undo, approval_view_audit. Include context fields: scope, count, filter. We'll add privacy-safe sampling.

nora: Perfect. I'll post updated frames and copy tokens later today. Thanks team :raised_hands:
